name: El Yunque National Forest
blurb: Rain-soaked peaks, coquí frogs and a parrot rebuilding after hurricanes.

tip.title: Silence the coquís
tip.text: Coquís eat huge numbers of arthropods. Set Common coquí to -100% and watch forest insects, then the predators that rely on frogs.

sources.title: USDA Forest Service: El Yunque National Forest

notes: The species list comes from GBIF occurrence records inside a circle around the park, so it can include nearby areas. Feeding links come from GloBI records and the sources listed where they state them; others are general ecology and are illustrative.

nodes.desc: Leaf-eating and litter-dwelling insects. A coqui study at El Yunque linked frog presence to fewer flying insects and far less leaf damage.
Small, very commonly recorded bird that takes nectar and fruit. GloBI records it eating fruit of several forest plants.
A fruit-eating bat recorded feeding on pumpwood. Fruit-eating bats help spread forest seeds.
An introduced omnivore that eats parrot eggs and chicks. It is in turn prey for the Puerto Rican boa.
An introduced predator that eats parrot eggs and chicks, and opportunistically takes coquís, according to the species accounts.
Warm, steady temperatures and light year-round drive growth, though cloud cover is frequent.
Shallow, acidic soils in the higher forest zones; nutrients come mainly from recycled leaf litter.

nodes.name: Decomposers
nodes.desc: Fungi, bacteria and litter invertebrates break down fallen leaves and wood and return nutrients to the soil.

story: El Yunque National Forest is a tropical rainforest in the northeast of the main island of Puerto Rico. Covering 28,516 acres of the Sierra de Luquillo mountain subrange, it is the only tropical rainforest in the U.S. National Forest System. It features multiple peaks and rivers, and provides a protected habitat for over 1,000 tree and plant species.
matters: It operates as an experimental forest providing scientific research on ecology, and it includes the Iguaca Aviary, which is dedicated to the preservation of the critically endangered Puerto Rican parrot.
